q: Biology is the study of living things.
e: This statement is true as biology encompasses the study of all organisms that live or have ever lived on Earth.

q: Biology only deals with animals and humans.
e: Biology also includes the study of plants, bacteria, fungi, and other organisms, not just animals and humans.

q: Living things include plants, animals, and other organisms.
e: This is accurate as living things, or organisms, encompass a wide variety of forms including plants, animals, and microorganisms.

q: Biology is unimportant in daily life.
e: Biology is fundamental to understanding food production and disease control, which are vital for our daily lives.

q: Biological advances have increased food production.
e: This statement is true; advancements in biology have led to improved agricultural practices and crop varieties.

q: The main branches of biology include physics and chemistry.
e: The main branches of biology include botany, zoology, and microbiology, not physics and chemistry.

q: Metabolism includes anabolism and catabolism.
e: Metabolism is indeed the sum of all chemical processes in an organism, which includes both anabolism and catabolism.

q: Growth in organisms is only seen as an increase in weight.
e: Growth in organisms is seen as an increase in size and weight, resulting from the use of food to develop structures.

q: Irritability refers to living things responding to stimuli.
e: This statement is true; irritability is the ability of living organisms to respond to environmental changes.

q: Reproduction is the production of a new generation of offspring.
e: Reproduction is indeed the process by which new individuals are produced, ensuring the continuation of a species.

q: All living things can reproduce only sexually.
e: Living things can reproduce both asexually and sexually, depending on the species.

q: Adaptability increases the chances of survival for species.
e: This statement is true; adaptability allows organisms to adjust to changes in their environment, enhancing survival.

q: Viruses are considered living organisms.
e: Viruses are not considered living organisms as they cannot carry out life processes independently.

q: The study of plants is known as botany.
e: Botany is the branch of biology that focuses on the study of plants.

q: Microbiology is the study of large organisms.
e: Microbiology is the study of microscopic organisms, not large organisms.

q: Cells contain DNA that carries biological information.
e: This statement is accurate; DNA molecules within cells carry the genetic information essential for life.

q: All living things are unicellular.
e: Living things can be unicellular or multicellular; for example, humans are multicellular organisms.

q: Taxonomy is the science of classification of organisms.
e: Taxonomy is indeed the science that deals with classifying living organisms into groups.

q: Only animals are classified into kingdoms.
e: Both plants and microorganisms, in addition to animals, are classified into kingdoms.

q: Eukarya includes organisms with prokaryotic cells.
e: The domain Eukarya includes organisms with eukaryotic cells, not prokaryotic.

q: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life in the world.
e: Biodiversity encompasses the variety of different species and ecosystems in the environment.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Animalia are autotrophic.
e: Organisms in the kingdom Animalia are heterotrophic, meaning they cannot produce their own food.

q: Taxonomy is essential for biology because it organizes living things into categories.
e: This statement is true; taxonomy helps in sorting and comparing different organisms.

q: Diversity of organisms is not important in biology.
e: The diversity of organisms is crucial in biology as it helps understand the complexity of life and ecosystems.

q: Taxonomy allows for easier study of millions of organisms.
e: This statement is accurate; taxonomy simplifies the study of numerous organisms by organizing them into manageable categories.

q: There are only two kingdoms in biological classification.
e: There are six kingdoms in biological classification, including Archaebacteria, Eubacteria, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

q: The hierarchical system of classification includes domains, kingdoms, and species.
e: This statement is true; the hierarchical classification system organizes life into domains, kingdoms, and further down to species.

q: Taxonomic hierarchy is fixed and does not change.
e: The taxonomic hierarchy is flexible and can change as new discoveries are made about organisms.

q: Linnaeus introduced the Binomial System of Nomenclature.
e: This statement is true; Linnaeus developed the system of naming organisms using two names, genus and species.

q: The first name in a binomial nomenclature is always lowercase.
e: In binomial nomenclature, the first name (genus) is always capitalized, while the second name (species) is lowercase.

q: Taxonomy helps in examining the evolutionary history of organisms.
e: This statement is accurate; taxonomy can reveal the evolutionary relationships among different organisms.

q: All organisms are classified into the same kingdom regardless of their characteristics.
e: Organisms are classified into different kingdoms based on their unique characteristics and traits.

q: The kingdom Fungi includes organisms that can photosynthesize.
e: The kingdom Fungi does not include photosynthetic organisms; fungi are heterotrophic.

q: The classification system is based on observable characteristics of organisms.
e: This statement is true; the classification system relies on the observable traits and characteristics of organisms.

q: Taxonomy does not consider evolutionary relationships.
e: Taxonomy does consider evolutionary relationships, which is essential for understanding the history of life.

q: The classification of organisms is important for scientific communication.
e: This statement is true; classification provides a universal language for scientists to communicate about organisms.

q: In taxonomy, similar species are grouped into different genera.
e: In taxonomy, similar species are grouped into the same genus.

q: The study of biodiversity is part of taxonomy.
e: This statement is accurate; taxonomy plays a role in understanding and documenting biodiversity.

q: Taxonomy is only concerned with living organisms.
e: Taxonomy also considers extinct organisms, as fossils are included in the classification system.

q: The classification system is static and does not adapt to new findings.
e: The classification system is dynamic and adapts as new scientific discoveries are made.

q: Taxonomy helps in identifying and naming new species.
e: This statement is true; taxonomy provides the framework for identifying and naming newly discovered species.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Plantae are unicellular.
e: The kingdom Plantae includes multicellular organisms, such as trees and flowering plants.

q: The kingdom Animalia includes both vertebrates and invertebrates.
e: This statement is accurate; the kingdom Animalia encompasses a wide variety of organisms, including both vertebrates and invertebrates.

q: Taxonomy only applies to animals and not to plants or fungi.
e: Taxonomy applies to all living organisms, including plants, fungi, and microorganisms.

q: A kingdom is a subdivision of a domain.
e: This statement is true; kingdoms are the next level of classification under domains.

q: There are five kingdoms of living things.
e: There are six kingdoms of living things: Archaebacteria, Eubacteria, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

q: Archaebacteria and Eubacteria are both prokaryotic kingdoms.
e: This statement is accurate; both kingdoms consist of prokaryotic organisms.

q: Eukarya includes only unicellular organisms.
e: The domain Eukarya includes both unicellular and multicellular organisms, such as plants and animals.

q: Viruses are included in the six kingdoms of living organisms.
e: Viruses are not classified within the six kingdoms as they are not considered living organisms.

q: Fungi can be unicellular or multicellular.
e: This statement is true; fungi can exist as single-celled organisms like yeast or multicellular organisms like mushrooms.

q: Plants are classified under the kingdom Animalia.
e: Plants are classified under the kingdom Plantae, not Animalia.

q: Animalia includes multicellular organisms that are heterotrophic.
e: This statement is accurate; organisms in the kingdom Animalia are multicellular and obtain energy by consuming other organisms.

q: Eubacteria are known for their complex cellular structure.
e: Eubacteria are prokaryotic and have a simpler cellular structure compared to eukaryotic organisms.

q: The kingdom Protista contains unicellular and colonial groups.
e: This statement is true; Protista includes a diverse range of unicellular and colonial organisms.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Fungi can photosynthesize.
e: Organisms in the kingdom Fungi do not have chlorophyll and cannot photosynthesize.

q: The kingdom Plantae consists of eukaryotic organisms.
e: This statement is accurate; Plantae includes eukaryotic organisms that are primarily autotrophic.

q: The characteristics of the kingdoms are the same for all.
e: Each kingdom has its own unique set of characteristics that differentiate it from others.

q: Viruses can reproduce independently outside of host cells.
e: Viruses cannot reproduce independently; they require host cells to replicate.

q: The kingdom Animalia includes organisms that are autotrophic.
e: Organisms in the kingdom Animalia are heterotrophic, meaning they cannot produce their own food.

q: The kingdom Protista includes both autotrophs and heterotrophs.
e: This statement is true; Protista includes organisms that can produce their own food as well as those that cannot.

q: All organisms in the kingdom Plantae are multicellular.
e: The kingdom Plantae includes both unicellular organisms like certain algae and multicellular plants.

q: The kingdom Fungi is characterized by the presence of chlorophyll.
e: Fungi lack chlorophyll and are unable to perform photosynthesis.

q: Eubacteria can reproduce asexually by fission.
e: This statement is accurate; Eubacteria commonly reproduce asexually through binary fission.

q: The classification of organisms is fixed and does not change over time.
e: The classification of organisms can change as new scientific discoveries are made.

q: Viruses are classified within the kingdoms of living organisms.
e: Viruses are not classified within the kingdoms as they do not meet the criteria for living organisms.
